# idea — raw notes (do not polish)

everyone has the same tools now. same model. same camera. same presets. and yet
the output is totally different. so the tool is not the differentiator anymore.
if it was, everyone would make the same thing.

thought: the tool removed the barrier, not the judgment. it made the first draft
free. the expensive part is knowing what's good.

drafts: what most people call "the hard part" (writing, drawing, building) is now
the cheap part. the hard part is taste. you can't prompt your way to taste.

hmm but is that true? like people said photoshop would make everyone a designer.
it didn't. it made good designers faster. same with the camera. same with this.

in-done-gone. make the point and exit. no wind-down. i keep writing conclusions
that just repeat the intro. cut them.

the studio ships late and proud. quality or nothing. a 300-word essay that shifts
something beats a 2000-word essay that fills space.

metaphor ideas:
- the Stradivarius thing is taken (violin makes no sound without a musician)
- the warehouse is taken
- maybe: everyone gets the same kitchen / the same palette — the meal is still
  different. or the same typeface, the same keys. a piano — everyone gets the
  same 88 keys. bach and the guy in the mall both have the same piano.
  the piano isn't the point. the player is. THE PIANO — that could work.
- or the blank canvas. or the same bricks.

ok i think the piano one. "everyone gets the same 88 keys."

also: this isn't a "tools are neutral" essay. it's harsher. the tool is a
filter for taste. it surfaces what you had all along. if you had nothing, the
tool shows you that too. that's the uncomfortable part. that's the contradiction
to open with.

open with the contradiction: you think the new tool makes you the writer. it
makes you the editor. and you were never trained to edit.

length ~500. single sentence paragraphs for the landings. no headers. no
"however". no "in conclusion". end on the piano image. don't explain it.

maybe mention: audiences can smell performative depth. they reward restraint.
this connects to "judgment over theater."

tangent — probably cut: i once spent a whole week on a reel that got 200 views
and a two-minute thought i typed in a doc that got read 10,000 times. the market
is not where you think it is.

ok. draft this. make it sharp.
